Procedural Programming
Procedural programming organizes a program around
procedures or functions that perform specific tasks.
Basic structured programming focuses on clear control
flow using sequence, selection, and repetition, while
procedural programming adds stronger organization by
dividing that logic into reusable functions.
The goal is to break a larger program into smaller
procedures that can be understood and tested
separately.

Focus on Functions
Procedural programming relies heavily on functions
to organize a program into smaller sections of
behaviour.
Each function usually receives data, performs a task,
and may return a result.
Procedural programming simply uses functions as
its main way of structuring program logic.

Atomization
Atomization means breaking a larger program into
smaller functions that each handle one part of the
problem.
Instead of keeping all of the program's logic
together, each major task becomes its own
procedure.
This makes the program easier to read, test, and
change.

Atomization
# Without Functions # With Functions
name = input("Enter your name: ") def get_name():
return input("Enter your name: ")
score1 = int(input("First score: "))
score2 = int(input("Second score: ")) def get_score():
return int(input("Enter a score: "))
average = (score1 + score2) / 2 def calculate_average(score1, score2):
return (score1 + score2) / 2
print(f"{name}'s average is {average}.")
def display_result(name, average):
print(f"{name}'s average is {average}.")
name = get_name()
score1 = get_score()
score2 = get_score()
average = calculate_average(score1, score2)
display_result(name, average)

One Function, One Task
A useful procedural programming guideline is that
each function should have one clear responsibility.
Functions can contain several lines of code, but
those lines should all contribute to the same task.
Separating unrelated jobs makes functions easier to
understand, reuse, and test.

Friendly Function Reminders – Type Hints
Always include type hints for your parameters and
return values.
: int : int) -> int

Friendly Function Reminders – Type Hints
Adding parameter type hints will help your code
editor warn you when you are putting invalid input
into a function.
Adding return type hints will help your code editor
warn you when you are incorrectly using the return
value.

Friendly Function Reminders – Docstrings
You should also always add correctly formatted
docstrings.
"""Calculate the area of a rectangle.
:param width: Width of the rectangle.
:param length: Length of the rectangle
:return: Area of the rectangle in units squared.
"""

Friendly Function Reminders – Docstrings
Docstrings will allow your code editor to explain your
own code to you later, even when you don’t have it
in front of you.
